briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 13, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Change and Increased Social Vulnerability
sections.content: News released today clearly demonstrates the direct damages and increased social vulnerability caused by climate change. 75% of surfing spots worldwide are now in a 'high-risk' state due to climate change and coastal development [1, 5], and the impacts of climate change are deeply penetrating daily life, as evidenced by persimmons barely bearing fruit on the persimmon tree-lined streets of Yeongdong County, Chungcheongbuk-do [98]. The insurance industry emphasized the crucial role of insurance in protecting 'climate-vulnerable groups' amidst increasing financial burdens due to the accelerating climate crisis [7, 12]. Furthermore, wildfires caused by El Niño in Indonesia have incinerated nearly 300 homes [130], and in the UK, at least 183 homes have been lost over the past 16 years due to coastal erosion [131], indicating ongoing physical damage from climate change.

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Efforts and Increased Citizen Participation
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts are underway to respond to the climate crisis and achieve carbon neutrality. Busan introduced climate change response tourism policies linked to the North Port redevelopment at an international forum [2, 13], and Gyeongnam Province is fully committed to overcoming climate change through a sea squirt aquaculture discussion [4]. Asan City is accelerating its transition to smart agriculture [9], and various local governments, including Buan, Gimpo, and Cheongju, are encouraging citizen participation by conducting carbon neutrality practice education for village elders and students [10, 16, 17]. In particular, Bucheon City recorded 1.11 million cumulative participations in its carbon neutrality practice platform, demonstrating active engagement from citizens and communities [24, 28, 29, 38, 41]. Interest in policy direction setting is also high, with calls for the National Pension Service to establish carbon neutrality targets and strengthen divestment from coal [20, 35].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges and Opportunities of Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is actively progressing, but simultaneously faces several challenges. Credit unions are expanding financial support for 'Sunshine Income Villages,' contributing to the revitalization of resident-led renewable energy projects [47, 58, 60, 63, 83, 85, 89, 90], and H-Energy and Peak Energy have embarked on expanding the RE100 market through joint development of rooftop solar nationwide [52, 72, 75, 76, 86, 92, 93, 96, 97]. However, concerns and conflicts regarding the generation of renewable energy-related waste are being raised in rural areas [48], and news has also emerged that costs have doubled due to the frequent operation of LNG power plants to compensate for the intermittency of renewable energy [49]. Furthermore, criticisms that Hanwha Solutions, which has championed 'next-generation solar,' has a renewable energy usage rate of only 1.3% [62], and the observation that 84% of potential solar areas in rural facilities remain unutilized [95], highlight the urgent need to enhance the effectiveness of renewable energy expansion policies.

sections.title: 🌍 Global Climate Governance and Discussion on the Role of AI
sections.content: The international community continues in-depth discussions on strengthening governance for climate change response, alongside the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI). The IPCC is facing pressure to delay the release of major global climate reports [100], and global civic organizations are calling for the suspension of SK Telecom's Myanmar greenhouse gas reduction project certification [11], indicating growing demands for credibility and transparency in climate action. Notably, concerns have been raised that the construction of AI data centers by global big tech companies is leading to the construction of new fossil fuel power generators, which could be interpreted as effectively abandoning or postponing carbon neutrality targets [19]. Meanwhile, Axa has stated that AI has surpassed climate change to become the top global threat [118], and alongside the possibility that AI chatbots could discourage climate action [113], the Cambodian Minister of Environment has requested AI support and technology transfer for climate change response [122, 128], indicating a growing awareness of AI's dual impact.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing simultaneously highlighted the severe reality of climate change, domestic and international efforts to overcome it, and the opportunities and challenges we face in renewable energy transition and AI technology utilization. We hope this information provides important insights for climate action. This concludes today's climate briefing.
